content: The MAS1 proto-oncogene, also known as the MAS1 proto-oncogene G protein-coupled receptor (MRGA, MAS, MGRA), encodes a protein in humans. This protein is classified as a receptor that is coupled to GTP-binding proteins. Its structure includes a conserved motif described as a 7-transmembrane segment, which is predicted to consist of hydrophobic regions forming membrane-spanning alpha-helices. The MAS1 protein is hypothesized to function as a receptor that, upon activation, modulates a critical component of a growth-regulating pathway, potentially leading to oncogenic effects. One of the known agonists of this receptor is angiotensin-(1-7). Antagonists include A-779, which is angiotensin-(1-7) with its C-terminal proline substituted by D-alanine, and D-Pro, which is angiotensin-(1-7) with its C-terminal proline replaced by D-proline. It is important to note that the MAS1 proto-oncogene (MAS1, MGRA) should not be confused with the MAS-related G protein-coupled receptor. The latter is believed to be activated by the ligand alamandine, which is generated either through the enzymatic action of ACE2 on Ang A or directly from angiotensin-(1-7).
